workload: Bootstrap of the median: draw 5000 with-replacement resamples of a length-200 sample and recompute the median on each, the realistic bootstrap-confidence-interval usage pattern. Baseline is the idiomatic numpy bootstrap loop (a Python for over B resamples, each a vectorized rng.integers resample + np.median). Throughput is resamples/sec.

methodology.aggregation: median of repeated timed runs, warm-up excluded
methodology.baseline_tool: numpy bootstrap loop (rng.integers + np.median per resample)

gate.note: The bootstrap loop is inherently sequential (each resample draws n indices from the RNG) and the per-resample statistic (a median, requiring a sort) cannot collapse into one vectorized numpy call, so the numpy loop pays per-resample interpreter overhead. The Rust loop draws and sorts natively. This is the idiomatic numpy bootstrap a competent user writes, not a rigged comparison.

latency.note: Single-resample cost ~2.5 us derived from the 400 Kresample/s rate, warm-up excluded; one resample-and-median is far under the sub-millisecond budget.

out_of_scope.resampling: batch bootstrap / permutation / cross-validation over a fixed sample, not streaming estimators (no online formulation)

known_debt: Only the bootstrap-of-the-median is benched as the family's gated hot path; permutation tests and k-fold cross-validation share the same sequential-loop advantage over an interpreted Python loop but are not separately gated.
